about: Revised names for the 20 theme clusters (20 Nov 2026). The model (embed_and_map.py) named each cluster from only the 20 titles nearest its centre, and several names fitted those titles but not the cluster. These names were written after reading, per cluster, the most distinctive title words, the most common keywords and OpenAlex topics, the most cited titles and a random sample of titles. build_site_data.py uses a revised name only when the model's name in the database is still model_name, so that a new clustering (with different clusters) is not given these names by mistake.

clusters.name: Core outcome sets and quality tools
clusters.desc: Delphi consensus studies that set core outcome sets and measurement standards (COSMIN), and tools to rate the quality and risk of bias of studies, mostly in medicine.

clusters.name: Open science and open access
clusters.desc: Open science in general: open access, open research culture, citizen science, and policies for and surveys of open practices across fields.

clusters.name: Mixed metascience topics
clusters.desc: A broad group without one shared subject: misconduct and retractions, bibliometric methods, p-values and Bayes factors, and research integrity.

clusters.name: Reporting guidelines (PRISMA, TRIPOD)
clusters.desc: Reporting guidelines and their extensions, such as PRISMA for systematic reviews, TRIPOD for prediction models and STARD for diagnostic accuracy studies.

clusters.name: Preregistration and trial registration
clusters.desc: Registering studies before they are done: clinical trial registries, preregistration in psychology and qualitative research, and whether registered outcomes match published ones.

clusters.name: Journals, preprints and science news
clusters.desc: How research is published and reported: journal practices, predatory journals, preprints, publishing during COVID-19, gender gaps among authors, and science journalism.

clusters.name: Research ethics and ethics review
clusters.desc: The ethics of doing research: ethics committees and review, informed consent, codes of conduct, and ethical questions in health, genomics, neuroscience and online research.

clusters.name: FAIR data principles
clusters.desc: Making research data findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable (FAIR): what the principles mean, how to measure them, data stewardship and the European Open Science Cloud.

clusters.name: Replicability and the replication crisis
clusters.desc: Papers about replication itself: the replication crisis, large replication projects, how to judge a replication, and computational reproducibility across fields.

clusters.name: Data sharing and data management
clusters.desc: Sharing and reusing research data: barriers and motives, data management plans, repositories, and the privacy and governance of health data.

clusters.name: Hypothesis testing and statistical evidence
clusters.desc: How to test hypotheses and weigh evidence: p-values and significance, Bayes factors, equivalence tests, choosing the alpha level, and planning sample sizes.

clusters.name: Clinical and brain research methods
clusters.desc: Methods papers within medicine, neuroscience and genetics: replication of genetic associations, reproducibility of neuroimaging, and measurement and bias in depression, pain and brain stimulation research.

clusters.name: Statistical methods and meta-analysis
clusters.desc: Statistical techniques and tutorials: meta-analysis and corrections for publication bias, sample sizes for prediction models, sequential designs, Bayesian model comparison, and many-analyst studies.

clusters.name: Research assessment, integrity and policy
clusters.desc: Science policy and research culture: how researchers are assessed and rewarded, research integrity and questionable practices, research funding, and the link between science and policy.

clusters.name: Research practices and theory in psychology
clusters.desc: Critiques of how psychological research is done: questionable research practices, researcher degrees of freedom, preregistration, measurement and theory building.

clusters.name: Peer review
clusters.desc: Peer review of papers and grant proposals: its quality, speed and biases, open peer review, registered reports, and the work of editors and reviewers.

clusters.name: Replications of specific findings
clusters.desc: Replication studies themselves: direct, conceptual and registered replications of particular findings, mostly in psychology and the behavioural sciences.

clusters.name: Bibliometrics and citation indicators
clusters.desc: Measuring science with publications and citations: impact indicators, the h-index, altmetrics, bibliographic databases and maps of science.

clusters.name: Reporting quality in clinical research
clusters.desc: Meta-research on published trials and systematic reviews: reporting quality, adherence to guidelines, publication bias, selective outcome reporting and spin.

clusters.name: AI and software tools in research
clusters.desc: Artificial intelligence and software in research: language models in writing and peer review, machine learning to screen literature for systematic reviews, and research software and metadata.
